0.headline: Zetwerk says poor customer quality, safety concerns led to civil infrastructure "mistake"
0.heading: Zetwerk says poor customer quality, safety concerns led to civil infrastructure "mistake"
0.intro: IPO-bound Zetwerk is exiting its civil infrastructure business due to customer quality and safety issues, taking financial hits before its public debut.
0.body:
IPO-bound Zetwerk said that its Civil Infrastructure Works business went wrong because of poor customer quality and safety concerns. As a result, the  manufacturing company decided to exit the segment ahead of its public market debut, taking a sharp hit to the company's financials.

“Safety first, which is where the civil infrastructure kind of went wrong. The customer quality there was horrible,” the firm's CEO Amrit Acharya said. “In the process of building things, we have made a couple of mistakes. Those mistakes we have shut down,” he added.

As a result of the discontinued operation, the firm took provisions both last year's financials and in Q1 numbers for FY27, which means there will be no pain carried forward after listing. "We wanted to do this before we go public, so that these are things in the past, not in the future. These are both non-cash adjustments. This does not affect the operating part of the business," Acharya added.

Zetwerk’s decision to exit its Civil Infrastructure Works business led to losses from discontinued operations of Rs 641 crore in FY26, up from Rs 156 crore reported in FY25.  For the quarter ended June for the current financial year, the company reported a loss of Rs 668.9 crore.

"Our restated loss for the period from discontinued operations in the three months period ended June 30, 2026 was primarily attributable to provisions for bad and doubtful debts and unbilled revenue," said the RHP.

As a result, the firm has decided to sell the operations for the Civil Infrastructure arm. The firm's red herring prospectus added that "the sale of the said business is expected to be completed within 12 months."

During the media interaction, the management also added that the mistakes were behind, and as a result, the business was strong with safeguards in place. “We built our business from scratch, from first principles,” Acharya said. “In the whole process of building, we have made a couple of mistakes. I think they are behind us.”

Zetwerk intends to raise Rs 5,012.3 crore via initial public offering (IPO) and is seeking a valuation of Rs 25,583.2 crore at the upper end of price band.

The IPO consisting fresh issuance of Rs 2,830 crore worth shares, and an offer-for-sale of 14.45 crore equity shares worth Rs 2,182.3 crore will open for public subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The anchor book will be opened for a day on October 14.

Zetwerk, which is backed by Peak XV Partners, Accel India, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, is likely to finalise IPO share allotment on October 21 and make its shares debut on the stock exchanges on October 23.

1.headline: Tonbo Imaging India IPO GMP jumps to 61% ahead of issue opening on October 15
1.heading: Tonbo Imaging India IPO GMP jumps to 61% ahead of issue opening on October 15
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Bengaluru-based defence electronics manufacturer Tonbo Imaging India is commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of nearly 61 percent ahead of its launch on October 15, according to market tracking platform InvestorGain.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Bengaluru-based defence electronics manufacturer Tonbo Imaging India is commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of nearly 61 percent ahead of its launch on October 15, according to market tracking platform InvestorGain.

The grey market premium stood at nearly 61 percent on the morning of October 13, indicating strong speculative interest ahead of the public issue. However, grey market premiums are unofficial indicators and do not guarantee listing gains.

The company has fixed the price band for its Rs 852.18-crore IPO at Rs 665–700 per share.

Read Also: From selling potatoes to supplying French fries to Burger King, KFC: How Haresh Karamchandani built Rs 1,500-crore HyFun Foods

The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The anchor book for institutional investors is scheduled to open on October 14.

The allotment is expected to be finalised on October 21, while the shares are likely to list on the BSE and NSE on October 23, subject to the final issue schedule.

The public issue comprises an offer for sale (OFS) of 1,21,74,046 equity shares, with no fresh issue component. At the upper end of the price band, the issue is valued at Rs 852.18 crore, implying a company valuation of around Rs 4,010 crore.

Since the IPO is entirely an OFS, Tonbo Imaging will not receive any proceeds from the issue. Instead, the net proceeds, after applicable expenses, will go to the shareholders selling their stakes.

Promoters Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar, Ankit Kumar and Cecilia D’Souza, along with existing investors such as CEAQ Technologies, Timothy Guy Mitchell, Artiman Partners LLC and Ramesh Radhakrishnan, are among the shareholders offloading their holdings.

Investors can bid for a minimum of 21 equity shares and in multiples of 21 shares thereafter. At the upper end of the price band of Rs 700 per share, the minimum investment required for one lot is Rs 14,700.

Check IPO News Here

The company has reserved 50 percent of the issue for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs) and 35 percent for retail individual investors.

JM Financial and IIFL Capital Services are the merchant bankers managing the IPO.

Tonbo Imaging reported a net loss of Rs 17.74 crore in the April–June quarter of FY27, while revenue stood at Rs 36 crore.

For FY26, the company’s profit after tax declined 30 percent to Rs 50.88 crore from Rs 72.76 crore in FY25. Its total income fell around 22.1 percent to Rs 369.94 crore in FY26 from Rs 474.39 crore in the previous financial year.

About Tonbo Imaging India

Incorporated in 2003, Tonbo Imaging designs and manufactures electro-optic and electronic systems for defence applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, handheld thermal imaging binoculars, targeting systems, missile seekers, fire-control systems and missile-guidance systems.

The company operates in the defence electronics segment, supplying technologies used in surveillance, reconnaissance, targeting and other military applications.

2.headline: HD Fire Protect IPO subscribed 15% so far on opening day; GMP at 32%
2.heading: HD Fire Protect IPO subscribed 15% so far on opening day; GMP at 32%
2.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of HD Fire Protect opened for subscription today, with the issue booked over 15 percent by 10:10 am on October 13, as per the NSE data.
2.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of HD Fire Protect opened for subscription today, with the issue booked over 15 percent by 10:10 am on October 13, as per the NSE data.

The Rs 712.1-crore IPO received bids for 30,29,840 shares against 1,84,20,492 shares on offer. Non-institutional investors (NIIs) led the demand, subscribing to their allotted portion 42 percent, while the retail investor category was subscribed 15 percent.

In the grey market, HD Fire Protect shares were commanding a premium of around 32 percent on the morning of October 13, according to market tracking platform InvestorGain. Grey market premiums are unofficial indicators of investor sentiment and do not guarantee listing gains.

Read Also: From struggling café to Rs 70-crore ice cream brand: How Narayan Rao built Bengaluru's popular 'Corner House Ice Creams'

HD Fire Protect has fixed a price band of Rs 258–271 per share for the public issue, which will remain open for subscription until October 15.

Investors can bid for a minimum of 55 equity shares and in multiples of 55 shares thereafter. At the upper end of the price band, the minimum investment for retail investors stands at Rs 14,905.

The allotment of shares is expected to be finalised on October 16, while the company's shares are scheduled to list on the stock exchanges on October 21.

The IPO is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of 2.62 crore equity shares, with no fresh issue component. Promoters Harish Narshi Dharamshi and his wife, Kusum Dharamshi, are selling their shares through the offering.

Since the issue comprises only an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds from the IPO. After deducting offer-related expenses, the proceeds will go to the selling shareholders.

The company has reserved 50 percent of the net offer, excluding the employee portion, for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). Non-institutional investors have been allocated 15 percent, while retail investors have been allotted 35 percent of the net offer.

HD Fire Protect has also reserved shares worth Rs 1.75 crore for eligible employees, who will receive a discount of Rs 25 per share to the final offer price.

Check IPO News Here

Ambit, Anand Rathi Advisors and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers for the issue.

HD Fire Protect reported a 6.4 percent year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 116.8 crore for the financial year ended March 2026. Revenue from operations rose 13.05 percent to Rs 489.3 crore during the same period.

For the June 2026 quarter, the company reported a profit of Rs 23.8 crore and revenue of Rs 109 crore.

The domestic market accounted for 65 percent of HD Fire Protect's revenue from operations in FY26, while international markets contributed the remaining 35 percent.
